name: Storm (rituals into a lethal Grapeshot)
description: A 60-card storm opponent that durdles for three turns, then chains rituals and cantrips into a lethal Grapeshot on turn 4. Teaches the clock: a combo deck's plan is a single turn, so either win first, hold a counterspell or discard for exactly that turn, or pressure their life total so they must go off early.

turns.boardSummary: 1 land, a cantrip; nothing on the battlefield

events.note: Cheap card selection. An empty battlefield on turn 1 against a deck full of instants and sorceries is the storm tell.

events.breakPoint: Decision point: this is the turn to deploy your fastest threat. Storm has no blockers; every point of damage now forces them to go off a turn early with a worse hand.

turns.boardSummary: 3 lands, Past in Flames in the graveyard, hand full of rituals

events.note: Loots away Past in Flames on purpose: it will be flashed back from the graveyard next turn.

turns.boardSummary: The combo turn: 4 lands, rituals chained, storm count 7, Grapeshot for eight

events.note: Ritual: pay two, add three. Storm count 1.
events.breakPoint: Counter the FIRST ritual, not the finisher: with the mana chain broken they cannot reach the storm count. If you have discard, take the finisher on turn 3, not the rituals.

events.note: Free spell that replaces itself: storm count 3, no mana lost.
Flashback from the graveyard (CR 702.34a): storm count 4. Every instant and sorcery in the graveyard gains flashback this turn, so the rituals come back.
Pyretic Ritual flashed back: storm count 5.
Desperate Ritual flashed back: storm count 6.
Manamorphose flashed back: storm count 7, and it draws a card.

Storm (CR 702.40a): when you cast it, copy it for each other spell cast before it this turn. Seven spells were cast before it, so seven copies plus the original: eight Grapeshots, one damage each, any targets.
events.breakPoint: The storm copies come from a triggered ability, so countering Grapeshot itself still leaves the copies. The realistic answers are earlier: discard the finisher on turn 3, counter the first ritual, or race. (A 'counter target triggered ability' effect stops the copies, but few decks run one.)

events.note: Eight damage to the face. From 20 this is lethal with the earlier chip damage; from 40 it is a wound, and they will rebuild for a second attempt.
